title: Tactical tempo pulseboard - ops sprint notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working pulseboard for short-window (1–4 week) product ops tracking that ties tactical roadmap slices to the most action-sensitive KPIs and an explicit fallback decision matrix. Use this doc during weekly cadence reviews (Tue 10:00 PT) and daily stand check-ins when signal drift is detected.

Why this is different
- Focus: short tempo (weekly) instead of long-term roadmap artifacts; designed to reduce decision latency and coordinate cross-functional quick fixes.
- Output-forward: each row ties to an explicit customer-facing behavior / risk metric and a minimal rollback/fallback action.
- Owner-first: every item has a named owner with an operational checklist so on-call and PMs can act without deep context.

Current sprint window: 2025-02-17 -> 2025-03-02
Last updated: 2025-02-28 (post-retro notes)

Topline objective for window
- Keep hosted API 99.95% 'golden route' throughput (p95 latency target) while onboarding 2 new open models into the catalog with canary traffic (10% per region). Minimize token-cost spike to +8% week-over-week.

Pulseboard rows (tactical roadmap slices -> signal -> owner -> action palette -> decision trigger)
1) Canary model onboarding (eu-west, us-west)
- Signal to watch: model error-rate (invalid outputs/structured failures) and user-facing hallucination report count (QA flagged). Metric owners: infra automated test + research evals.
- Owner: Diego Alvarez (solutions eng)
- Ops checklist: deploy canary, enable structured logs, set eval harness to run nightly 1k prompts, route 10% traffic.
- Action palette (if signal degrades): 1) throttle to 2% traffic, 2) switch traffic to verified model variant, 3) trigger rollback.
- Decision trigger: nightly eval failure >3% regression on quality suite OR customer QA tickets >5 in 24h -> immediate throttle and notify PM+SRE.

2) Token-cost optimization trial (batching + prefix cache heuristics)
- Signal to watch: tokens-per-response (avg), cost/manhattan to baseline, response latency p95.
- Owner: Priya Nair (product ops)
- Ops checklist: enable batching profile X, enable prefix cache for repeat prompts, monitor cost dashboard, document changes in config repo.
- Action palette: 1) reduce batch size, 2) disable prefix cache for latency-sensitive paths, 3) revert to previous config.
- Decision trigger: >12% cost increase week-over-week with >5ms added latency on p95 -> rollback to previous config and open retrospective.

3) Dedicated pool autoscale tuning for reserved customers
- Signal to watch: queued requests per GPU, scale latency, SLA breach count.
- Owner: Liam O'Connor (platform eng liaison)
- Ops checklist: apply autoscale curve A, set cooldown 90s, annotate incidents, run 4h soak test.
- Action palette: 1) widen autoscale headroom, 2) escalate to SRE, 3) temporarily shift small customers to spare pool.
- Decision trigger: SLA breach >3 customers in 6h or queue depth sustained >X -> open incident, run pool-shift.

4) Console rollout: model rollout controls visible in UI (per-route toggles)
- Signal to watch: permission errors, control-plane latency, adoption by beta customers.
- Owner: Maya Chen (product ops)
- Ops checklist: verify feature flag toggles, enable rollout telemetry, test rollback flows, update help doc.
- Action palette: 1) disable UI toggle, 2) revert control-plane change, 3) escalate to frontend oncall.
- Decision trigger: >2 beta customers report inability to change toggles or UI errors for >1h -> rollback feature toggle and notify beta list.

Micro-KPIs to surface every stand (short list, data refresh cadence in parens)
- Golden-route p95 latency (5m)
- Error-rate (all non-2xx) (5m)
- Token-cost delta vs baseline (24h)
- Canary quality regressions (nightly)
- SLA breach count (1h)
- Customer QA tickets labelled 'model-hallucination' (real-time)
- Critical regressions triage time (MTTR) (rolling 7d)

Weekly KPI dashboard snapshot (to paste into meeting notes)
- p95 latency: 142ms (target <=150ms)
- Error-rate: 0.12% (target <=0.2%)
- Token-cost delta: +6.8% WoW (target <=+5%) -> flagged
- Canary regression count: 2 / nightly suite (trigger threshold 3)
- SLA breach: 0 active
- Open hallucination tickets: 3 (escalated)
- Mean time to rollback (last 30d): 28m

Fallback decision matrix (compact cheat sheet)
- Severity A (customer-facing outage / SLA broken): immediate incident page; route to incident commander (SRE) -> execute pool failover -> notify CSMs and customers.
- Severity B (meaningful degradation: p95 latency > target or token-cost spike > threshold): throttle canaries, engage product ops + platform, prepare rollback plan within 2 hours.
- Severity C (quality drift without outage): run targeted eval suite, reduce canary traffic, coordinate with model QA for retrain or prompt-engineering patch.

Owner roster and escalation contacts (primary -> backup -> pager)
- Diego Alvarez -> Priya Nair -> SRE oncall (pager id)
- Priya Nair -> Maya Chen -> Product oncall
- Liam O'Connor -> Platform lead -> Infra oncall

Weekly ritual and meeting agenda (Tue 10:00 PT, 45 mins)
1) 10m: Pulse readout (top 3 signals, owners speak)
2) 10m: Tactical blockers and quick fixes (decisions to take now)
3) 10m: Escalations and customer impact mapping
4) 10m: Action assignment + quick retro on previous window
5) 5m: Parking lot items and next steps

Retro notes (2025-02-24)
- What worked: the nightly eval harness caught a structured-output bug before customer impact; quick throttle path was clear.
- What didn't: cost experiment rollout lacked a canary rule for the high-cost tenant type -> caused manual rollback.
- Action items from retro:
  - Add tenant-type label to cost experiment canary (owner: Priya, due: 2025-03-03)
  - Document rollback playbook for prefix-cache (owner: Diego, due: 2025-02-28)
  - Add a per-tenant cost alert to the dashboard (owner: Liam, due: 2025-03-05)

Open questions / parking lot
- Should we standardize the 10% canary rule across regions or allow per-model tuning? (PM + Research decision)
- Do we need a separate minimal runbook for regulated on-prem customers when canarying new quantized artifacts?

Quick links & dashboards (paste during meeting)
- Live p95 dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/p95
- Cost delta sheet: https://sheets.redwood/cost-delta-weekly
- Canary eval logs: https://logs.redwood/canary-evals/nightly
- Incident runbook index: https://confluence.redwood/incident-runbooks

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep the pulseboard trimmed to 3 active rows maximum; everything else goes into the backlog lane.
- When in doubt, prefer throttle+monitor over full rollback for low-severity drift.
- Capture the smallest reproducible eval prompt for any regression before opening a full ticket.

Appendix: Minimal rollback checklist (copyable)
- Notify stakeholders (thread + #incidents)
- Throttle traffic to 2% for the canary
- Collect full logs for last 1h
- If persistent after 30m: execute rollback (route to previous model variant)
- Confirm baseline metrics recovered for 60m
- Post-incident: write 1-paragraph blameless summary and assign retro owner

-- end of working notes --
